newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates rise with new reserve period.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates rise with new reserve period.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates rose at mid-session on Monday as banks stopped liquidating excess funds with the beginning of a new reserve period, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate was at 5.979 percent against Saturday's 5.445 close -- far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper rising to 6.00-6.05 percent from 6.00.
Dealers said they expected the rates to hover around the six percent level.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0860-0865 against 6.1040. -- James Lin (5080815)
